reasons: The cited text substantively supports the compliant classification: §7.5(a) requires cooperation in an orderly transition, §7.5(b) requires transfer of funds and delivery of the Receivable Files and records to the Successor Servicer, §7.5(c) puts transition expenses on the outgoing Servicer, and §7.3 keeps the Servicer performing until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement — assistance and data return are present and exceed the fallback duration.
Walk-away territory (no data return, or immediate deletion of data) is absent; §3.10(f) adds a parallel file-delivery obligation for the Custodian at its own expense.

The failed deterministic 'data return/transition present' regex is a phrasing artifact — this ABS agreement uses 'Receivable Files', 'accounts and records' and 'Successor Servicer' rather than 'data export/return' vocabulary — so it does not undercut the substance.

Shortfalls versus the model language ('as soon as practicable' rather than a hard 30-day outside date, no deletion-and-certification mechanic, carve-outs for proprietary servicing software and confidentiality/privacy-restricted items) are correctly noted in the rationale as minor sub-elements rather than flagged as a deviation, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics.
No redline or counterparty comment is proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding retained as internal evidence.
